clue.text: Occasionally somebody catches cold to some extent

indicators.note: catches means the word for somebody holds the cold abbreviation inside it

parts.note: somebody can be one, as in 'one never knows'
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to some extent means in a way, partly

explanation.surface: Now and then someone picks up a mild chill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means from time to time, now and then, without regularity.

clue.text: Love girl well

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O
Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lover tells a girl all is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying a person is fine or in good health.

clue.text: In disappointment, comfort the cabinet

explanation.surface: Ministers let down by events are cheered by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone let down is to cheer them; a radio or gramophone cabinet is also called by the same name.

clue.text: Drains immune to change in unseasonably warm weather

indicators.note: to change tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Drainage that refuses to alter during a hot autumn spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' makes an anagram of DRAINS IMMUNE; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a spell of warm sunny weather late in the year, after summer has gone.

clue.text: A river bird, jolly familiar

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps
the mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A bird by a river looks cheerful and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is not an adjective here: in naval slang a Jolly is a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with linked arms shows intimacy, so the phrase describes a close, friendly relationship.

clue.text: Cancel the jacket for author's first book

indicators.note: the word for cancel acts as a jacket, wrapped around a letter

parts.note: to annul a contract is to cancel it

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word author's

explanation.surface: A writer withdraws the dust cover from their debut novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' looks like a book's dust jacket, but it is the container signal; 'the' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly hardback publication, especially a children's one, is a kind of book.

clue.text: I twice set a bird

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used as a musical direction to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a bird two times.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is a music term meaning play the passage again; 'set' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading species sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Agent in trouble hit out on all sides

indicators.note: on all sides means the word for hit out surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to biff someone is to hit out at them
to ail is to be in trouble or unwell

explanation.surface: An agent in difficulty lashes out at everyone around.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff's officer who serves writs and seizes goods acts as an agent of the court.

clue.text: You get sound travelling from it, sound to impress with beauty

definitions.text: You get sound travelling from it

indicators.note: the second sound signals that we hear these words spoken rather than see them written

parts.note: to slay is to impress hugely, and a belle is a beauty

explanation.surface: A ringing noise as you travel, and a voice meant to impress a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'sound' is part of the definition, the noise you hear as a sledge moves; the second is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jingling bell is hung on a horse-drawn sledge, so it rings as the sledge travels.

clue.text: In old age, bishop follows girl by car

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Odo was the Bishop of Bayeux, half-brother of William the Conqueror
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: Late in life, a churchman trails a young woman in a small car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' and 'by' place the pieces in order; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for in the year of our Lord is used jokingly to mean advancing years.

clue.text: Be wrong about …

indicators.note: about tells us the word for wrong turns round to be read backwards

parts.note: evil is moral wrong

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken concerning a matter that continues in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, a synonym in the sense of having life.

clue.text: Avoiding familiarity and finally succeeding, learnt maths with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty signals the letters struggle into a new order
finally picks the closing letter of the word succeeding

explanation.surface: In the end, a student mastered mathematics with a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' makes an anagram of G (from 'finally succeeding') plus LEARNT MATHS; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping someone at a distance means refusing closeness or intimacy.

clue.text: … kind of seat found in lots of amphitheatres

indicators.note: found in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A type of seating seen in many ancient arenas.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the one before but adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholstered settee is a long seat for two or more people.

clue.text: Discovering uranium missing — it could have been a disaster

definitions.text: it could have been a disaster

indicators.note: missing means the chemical symbol is removed from the longer word

parts.note: unearthing something is discovering it
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Finding the nuclear fuel gone might have been catastrophic.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is a close call that almost became a catastrophe.

clue.text: Koala could be in trouble

parts.note: a koala lives high in a eucalyptus, and the idiom for being stuck in difficulty names exactly that perch

explanation.surface: An Australian marsupial may be in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a fix, and a eucalyptus is literally where a koala sits.

clue.text: As result of a repulse, will …

indicators.note: result of signals that the letters are the product of rearranging the words that follow

explanation.surface: Being turned back leaves someone with a strong wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result of' makes an anagram of A REPULSE; 'As' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's wish or desire, as in 'at Her Majesty's pleasure', is their will.

clue.text: … start to park in front of Judge Jack's house

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the word park

parts.note: a referee, ref, judges a match
a jack or jack tar is a sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: Parking outside a judge's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' puts the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory-made home assembled on site, common in post-war Britain, is a type of dwelling.

clue.text: God overwhelmed by prayer in excess

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the god's name is swamped inside the word for prayer

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request or prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A deity swamped by too many supplications.
explanation.definitionFit: A superabundance means too much of something, a surplus.

clue.text: You're told to stick me down

indicators.note: you're told signals that the words are heard, not read

parts.note: glue me means stick me

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to fasten themselves to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means low in spirits, dejected.

clue.text: Choose one parent, that's best

parts.note: to opt is to choose
I is the Roman numeral one
mum is a mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Picking one mother is the top choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The most favourable condition or amount is the ideal one.

clue.text: Drawback about girl meeting fellow for a drink

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the other pieces
back tells us the word for draw is read in reverse

parts.note: to lug is to draw or haul
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A disadvantage concerning a girl dating a man, enough to drive one to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one word meaning a snag, but it splits: 'back' reverses the word for Draw, and 'about' wraps that round the girl and fellow; 'meeting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount a tumbler holds is a measure of a drink.

clue.text: A small number, it's said, getting weary, abstained

indicators.note: it's said signals that the number is heard, not spelt

parts.note: four is a small number
to bore someone is to weary them

explanation.surface: Several people, reportedly tired, chose not to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from something is the same as holding back from it.

clue.text: Bandage man after blow

indicators.note: after means the man comes behind the blow in the answer

parts.note: a swat is a sharp blow
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man is bandaged up after being struck.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap or swaddle something is to bind it like a dressing.

clue.text: Common sense could be worth time

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Practical wisdom may be worth the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Native good sense, the practical intelligence one is born with.

clue.text: Each is short of five — that's strange

indicators.note: is short of means the Roman five is taken away from the word for each

parts.note: every means each
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Every one falls short of five, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the older spelling of eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny and weird, giving a sense of unease.

clue.text: Make an arrangement when season's over

indicators.note: over tells us the word for season is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: tide is an old word for a season, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Plans are made once the holiday period ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare a text or film for release is to put it into shape.

clue.text: Something leading up to swindle

explanation.surface: A con trick that leads on to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope gives access to a higher level; it is also slang for a fraudulent scheme.

clue.text: Keep confusing long and short division when beginning

indicators.note: confusing means the letters are jumbled together
when beginning picks just the opening letter of the word division

explanation.surface: Keep confusing long and short division at the start of maths lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' makes an anagram of LONG SHORT; 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun, a castle's tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, its fortress.

clue.text: Award for farewell appearances in prize from film industry

indicators.note: farewell appearances are final ones, so take the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A trophy for final performances in a cinema prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A statuette given for television achievement in the United States.

clue.text: Impartiality displayed by some soldiers

explanation.surface: Even-handedness shown by a squad of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloofness or impartiality is one sense; a unit of troops detached for a duty is the military sense.
